name: Solenne Spire Biosync Executive Day Suit
description: Power does not need to announce itself, but it does not mind being recognized. The Solenne Spire Biosync Executive Day Suit is a three-piece ensemble in midnight charcoal cashmere-silk composite, cut bespoke to the wearer's biometric profile and updated seasonally via Solenne's mobile atelier service. The jacket is structured but not stiff — the internal posture-enhancement mesh activates subtly when the wearer sits or stands, keeping the shoulders square and the silhouette commanding without any effort. The fabric itself is privacy-weave certified: a woven Faraday mesh integrated at the panel seams blocks passive biometric scanning, thermal imaging, and BCI sniffing from outside parties. A collarless, banded-neck vest in matching cashmere-silk sits beneath, piped in a single thread of deep copper at the edges — the only ornamentation visible to the room. The dress shirt beneath is spun from a temperature-regulating microfiber that reads ambient conditions and adjusts breathability in real time, collarless and smooth, no visible buttons. Trousers are wide-legged and high-waisted with a single rear inverted pleat, gene-compatible with a discreet rear vent panel that accommodates tails up to a standard geneware diameter of 6cm, finished with a self-fastening magnetic closure invisible at the waistband. Footwear is a pair of bespoke Solenne lacquered oxfords in midnight charcoal, hand-lasted, with a micro-heel that adjusts height by 1.2cm via a concealed pneumatic sole — a detail so subtle it is almost insulting that it exists at all. No badge. No lanyard. No logo. This person does not need to prove they belong.
functionality: Passive posture correction via internal mesh, privacy-weave blocks biometric and BCI scanning, temperature-regulating shirt fabric, gene-compatible rear vent panel for tail accommodation, pneumatic adjustable heel, RFID-null waistband, augmentation clearance at collar and cuff for neural port and wrist chrome access
what_it_says: This person sets the dress code. They do not follow it. The absence of branding is itself the most powerful signal in the room — only someone who does not need external validation removes all external markers. The posture mesh means they always look like the most composed person present, even when they are not. The privacy-weave means no one in the room knows their heart rate, their implant load, or their BCI activity. They are unknowable by design.
worn_by: old-money inheritors with active board seats
manufacturer: Solenne Atelier — bespoke, by appointment only, Spire-access required for fitting
price_range: Φ28,000–Φ55,000 per commissioned set; seasonal update service Φ4,000/quarter
story_hooks: The privacy-weave in this suit is blocking something it shouldn't be able to block — someone has had the fabric upgraded with a classified-grade signal suppressor, and the person who installed it has since disappeared.

A Tier 3 character is handed this suit and told to wear it to a meeting, impersonating the executive who owns it. The posture mesh begins correcting them in ways that feel deeply wrong — the suit was fitted to someone with a very different body, and the corrections are painful.

The pneumatic heel adjustment is a dead giveaway — someone who knows Solenne's manufacturing history recognizes the micro-click when the wearer shifts their weight, and now they know exactly which production quarter this suit was commissioned in, which narrows down the owner's identity to fewer than eight people.
